title: Kernel stitch notes: staggered prefill experiments diary
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact standup + experiment diary for the staggered prefill experiments (iter-3). Goal was to reduce token tail latency regressions observed in mixed small/long request workloads while preserving batching efficiency and KV hit rate. Notes are informal — decisions and follow-ups at the bottom.

Attendees (standup):
- Leah (owner)
- Ravi (kernel lead)
- Clara (KV cache)
- Marcus (benchmarking / perf)

Summary of last week:
- Ran iter-2 with a single global prefill gate; observed 6% p99 increase on user mix with 30% long-context requests. Batch efficiency unchanged but coalescing delayed for small requests behind long-prefill tasks.
- Identified that current per-worker prefill scheduling has no aging priority — long-prefill tasks can block short ones inside the same coalescer window.

What we experimented (iter-3):
1) Staggered prefill windowing
   - Approach: split the coalescer window into micro-windows (2–4 ms slices) and assign incoming requests a micro-window based on estimated prefill length. Short prefill requests get earlier micro-windows.
   - Kernel changes: small patch to the kernel scheduler that tags requests with an estimated prefill class using the request metadata header (client-side provided estimate + server-side conservative upper bound). Added prefill_class field to the in-flight descriptor.
   - KV change: allow prefetch workers to check micro-window tag before allocating KV prefill slot.

2) Light-weight aging token in queue
   - Approach: when a request waits >10ms in the coalescer, its priority is bumped once. Implemented as a fast-path atomic increment on the per-queue priority counter.

3) Soft prefetch abort on overrun
   - If a prefill candidate's runtime estimate > 2x median observed, we abort prefill and fall back to on-demand token fetch to avoid long blocking.

Quick results (benchmarks run by Marcus):
- Workload: 70% short (128 tokens), 30% long (4096 tokens) synthetic mix.
- Baselines: iter-2 baseline vs iter-3 patches on same infra.
- P50: unchanged (~18 ms). P95: improved by ~4%. P99: improved by ~3% (noted that in a few runs P99 variance high — see linked artifacts).
- KV hit-rate: negligible change (-0.6pp).
- Batching efficiency: small drop in mean batch fill (2.2% reduction) but end-to-end CPU/GPU utilization identical due to reduced tail retries/overruns.

Observed anomalies / bugs:
- Race in descriptor update (kernel): under heavy load, the prefill_class write and subsequent priority bump can interleave with queue flush path causing descriptor to be enqueued without class tag. Repro steps attached to GH PR.
- Prefetch worker memory leak: Clara observed a small leak (~4MB/min) when prefetch abort path was exercised; root cause is dropped completion callbacks not freeing buffer.
- Benchmark flakiness: occasional outlier runs where P99 regresses to baseline or worse; likely due to network jitter between coalescer and prefetch workers. Marcus to add network-in-band checks.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Ravi: add an atomic descriptor init path to eliminate prefill_class race (PR-4821 comment thread). ETA: 2026-05-18.
- Clara: fix completion callback leak in prefetch worker; add unit test and run memcheck. ETA: 2026-05-17.
- Marcus: extend benchmark harness to include in-band latency markers + more seeds; re-run nightly with stress harness. ETA: 2026-05-16 (first re-run).
- Leah: synthesize canary policy for rolling out staggered prefill to 10% of traffic on staging clusters; write rollback criteria. ETA: 2026-05-20.
- Team: evaluate trade-offs on batch fill reduction vs tail improvement and decide whether to keep micro-windowing. Discuss in next sync.

Discussion notes from meeting:
- Trade-off posture: We agreed that small batch fill loss is acceptable if P99 and tail jitter improve and if KV hit-rate stable. But we need telemetry to attribute customer impact.
- Observability: add per-request prefill_class tag to traces and surface distribution in Console (per-route histogram). Clara to drive Console metric PR with product-observability.
- Client-cooperation: we noted some clients can supply expected context length; field-team to draft best-practice header for client-supplied estimates. This will improve micro-window assignment quality.

Decisions made:
- Proceed with iter-3 approach to the canary stage (10% traffic) once race and leak are fixed.
- Keep soft prefetch abort at 2x median for now; we may tune to 1.5x if staging telemetry shows conservative firing.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we safely decline batch fill further under some routes to prioritize latency for others? (e.g., route-level latency SLO overrides). Product wants a config knob.
- Should we expose a per-customer prefill aggressiveness knob for Dedicated plans? Legal for now — product to propose scope.

Meeting snippets / quick logs:
- 10:03 — Ravi: "saw the race in the wild, reproducible at 90% qps"
- 10:12 — Marcus: "bench flakiness correlates with a couple of ipsec route changes, adding trace markers"
- 10:30 — Clara: "prefetch abort path fixed locally, pushing test"

Appendix: quick local repro steps (short)
1) Launch coalescer with micro-windowing enabled (feature flag: prefill.microwindow=true)
2) Run synthetic mix with 30% long requests (script: bench/mix-long-short.sh --seed 42)
3) Observe p99 and run memcheck on prefetch worker (stress 60s).

File notes / provenance:
- Drafted during standup; refined with Marcus' benchmark output and PR logs. Will convert to Confluence after canary if decision goes final.

If you pick this up: read the GH PR and the attached flamegraphs in the linked artifacts before running the canary.

-- Leah
